points_of_interest.note: Village centre from OpenStreetMap. The exact slide (Donuz-Oi section) is not mapped yet.

event.label: Landslide, about 42.8 thousand m³ of ground on the move

source.name: Ministry of Emergency Situations via Economist.kg, 12 Oct 2026

facts.text: About 42,800 m³ of ground started moving on 10 October 2026 around 14:00, at roughly 1.1 m per hour, with a 220 m crack.

source.name: Ministry of Emergency Situations via Economist.kg, 12 Oct 2026

facts.text: 11 people from two families were evacuated; two houses lie in the slide's possible path.

source.name: Ministry of Emergency Situations via Economist.kg, 12 Oct 2026

facts.text: The Ylai-Talaa–Gülchö road (detour at km 22–23), a substation and power lines are at risk.

source.name: Ministry of Emergency Situations via Economist.kg, 12 Oct 2026

place.explore: A slope above Toguz-Bulak village in the mountains of Osh region began to slide on 10 October 2026.
place.research: Donuz-Oi section, Kara-Kulja district. ~42.8 thousand m³, ~1.1 m/h, 220 m tension crack (MChS).

rain.explore: Rainfall data for this window is not added yet.
rain.research: TODO(story): add the IMERG series and describe it.

radar.explore: NISAR's L-band radar sees the ground through cloud, day and night, every 12 days on this track.
radar.research: NISAR L2 GCOV, track 156 ascending, frame 022, 20 m pixels, HH and HV, provisional calibration (CRID P05023).

tracking.explore: We compare the last radar pass before the slide (29 Sep) with the first one after it (11 Oct).
tracking.research: HH change between consecutive passes, averaged over 3×3 pixels; |ΔHH| above 3 dB is coloured.

exposure.explore: Two houses, a road, a substation and power lines are in the slide's possible path.
exposure.research: From the Ministry of Emergency Situations report; no building count from maps yet.

limitations: The first pass after the slide is about 16 hours after it began; later movement is not in this stack.
A ~43,000 m³ slide covers only a few hectares, a few dozen 20 m pixels at most.
Provisional NISAR calibration (P05023). Validated products start 21 Oct 2026 and are not mixed in.
The village point is from OpenStreetMap; the slide outline is not mapped yet, so no validation numbers.
